extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals, prospective CJR-X participants, healthcare administrators, legal/compliance officers, and other providers or suppliers considering participation in CJR-X or entering financial arrangements with CJR-X participants
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed CMS rule text specifying definitions, permitted financial arrangements (sharing arrangements), collaborator eligibility, documentation, program-integrity safeguards, and limits governing gainsharing and alignment payments under the CJR-X model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on overlap with ACO/total cost of care models
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow beneficiaries aligned to a total cost of care model (e.g., Medicare Shared Savings Program or other ACO initiatives) who also initiate a CJR-X episode to be included in CJR-X and for both participants to retain savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: simplifies participation by avoiding complexities in prior models about when episodes trigger or are excluded; fosters cooperative relationships between accountable care and CJR-X participants; can strengthen episode volume for CJR-X participants to mitigate low-volume challenges. CMS acknowledges some ACOs may prefer exclusion but believes combined models benefit beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: No concurrent participation with TEAM
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X would not allow concurrent participation with the TEAM model; TEAM and CJR-X both test bundled payments for LEJRs and run concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: TEAM participants would be excluded from CJR-X participation for LEJR episodes at TEAM hospitals (TEAM supersedes CJR-X). §512.630(e) proposal: if a beneficiary in a TEAM episode has an LEJR at a CJR-X hospital during TEAM's 30‑day post-discharge, that LEJR will not initiate a CJR‑X episode and the spending will be included in the TEAM episode. Conversely, if a beneficiary in a CJR‑X episode has a procedure at a TEAM hospital that would initiate TEAM during the CJR‑X 90‑day post‑discharge, that procedure would not initiate TEAM and spending would be included in CJR‑X. Rationale: hold anchoring provider accountable, avoid duplicative calculations and double payment, and limit beneficiary confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “CJR‑X collaborator” (eligible types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define “CJR‑X collaborator” as specified Medicare‑enrolled providers/suppliers or entities participating in Medicare ACO initiatives that may be CJR‑X collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed types include: SNF, HHA, LTCH, IRF, physician, nonphysician practitioner, therapist in private practice, CORF, outpatient therapy providers, PGP, hospital, CAH, NPPGP, TGP, and Medicare ACO. CMS seeks comment on adding other providers (e.g., REHs, rural clinics, FQHCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “sharing arrangement” and payment types
rubrics_metrics.description: A sharing arrangement is a financial arrangement between a CJR‑X participant and a CJR‑X collaborator whose sole purpose is making gainsharing payments or alignment payments under CJR‑X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where payment from participant to collaborator is a gainsharing payment; payment from collaborator to participant is an alignment payment. A CJR‑X participant must not make a gainsharing payment or receive an alignment payment except in accordance with a sharing arrangement. Sharing arrangements must comply with §512.670(b) and all applicable laws and fraud and abuse rules; must be documented in writing and made available to CMS upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for written policies for selecting collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must develop, maintain, and use written policies for selecting individuals and entities to be CJR‑X collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria must include the quality of care delivered by the potential collaborator and must not be based directly or indirectly on the volume or value of referrals or business generated by or between the parties. Participants must also consider anticipated contribution to the participant's performance in the model when selecting collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance program oversight for sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CJR‑X participant enters a sharing arrangement, its compliance program must include oversight of sharing arrangements and compliance with model requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will monitor compliance (documentation requests, interviews, site visits). Proposal also requires CJR‑X collaborators to have a compliance program overseeing the sharing arrangement. CMS seeks comment on the burden for small providers and whether alternative compliance requirements are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board/governing body oversight responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The board or other governing body of the CJR‑X participant is responsible for overseeing the participant's participation in the model and its arrangements with CJR‑X collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight responsibilities include payment of gainsharing payments, receipt of alignment payments, and use of beneficiary incentives. Sharing arrangements must be documented in writing and made available to CMS upon request as part of monitoring and compliance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing arrangement general program integrity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing arrangements must comply with applicable provisions of the proposed rule, beneficiary notification requirements, access to records, record retention, and participation in monitoring, evaluation, compliance, and enforcement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties (including contractors/subcontractors and collaboration agents) must comply; providers/suppliers party to arrangement must meet Medicare provider enrollment requirements (§424.500) and have valid TIN/NPI during term of the sharing arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness and timing of sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing arrangements must be voluntary, without penalty for nonparticipation, in writing, signed by the parties, and entered into before care is furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries under the arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: preserve beneficiary freedom of choice, access, and quality of care. Agreements must set mutually agreeable terms intended to guide future model performance, not reflect known past performance outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing arrangement must not risk beneficiary access, choice, or quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing arrangements must not pose a risk to beneficiary access, beneficiary freedom of choice, or quality of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangement terms must not induce reduction or limitation of medically necessary services, nor restrict collaborator's ability to make decisions in beneficiaries' best interests (including selection of devices, supplies, and treatments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of written sharing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: A written sharing arrangement must specify the arrangement's purpose/scope; identities and obligations of parties; date; management and staffing info; and financial/economic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial/economic terms must include: eligibility criteria for gainsharing and alignment payments; frequency of payments; methodology and accounting formula for determining gainsharing payments solely based on quality and provision of CJR‑X activities; methodology for alignment payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “CJR‑X activities”
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X activities are activities related to promoting accountability for quality, cost, and overall care for CJR‑X beneficiaries and performance in the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: managing and coordinating care; encouraging investment in infrastructure and redesigned care processes; carrying out obligations/duties under the model. CMS seeks comment on this inclusive definition as capturing direct care and care redesign contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gainsharing payment origin and form restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Gainsharing payments must be derived solely from a CJR‑X participant's reconciliation payment amounts, internal cost savings, or both; distributed annually (no more than once per calendar year); not loans/advances/payments for referrals; and clearly identified as gainsharing at time paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: program integrity safeguard aligning gainsharing with model incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conditions for gainsharing payments (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for gainsharing payments is conditioned on (1) meeting quality of care criteria and (2) provision of CJR‑X activities during the performance year for which the participant earned the reconciliation payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality criteria will be included in the sharing arrangement and mutually agreed by parties. For collaborators other than PGPs/NPPGPs/TGPs, the collaborator must have directly furnished a billable item/service to a beneficiary during the performance year for which the reconciliation payment was earned (hospital/CAH/post‑acute considered 'directly furnished' if they billed for an item/service).

rubrics_metrics.name: PGP/NPPGP/TGP-specific gainsharing eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: PGPs, NPPGPs, and TGPs must have billed for an item or service rendered by one or more members to a CJR‑X beneficiary during the episode attributed to the same performance year to be eligible for gainsharing or subject to alignment payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, because they do not directly furnish items/services as entities, they must have contributed to CJR‑X activities and been clinically involved in beneficiary care during the episode attributed to the performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gainsharing methodology requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any gainsharing payments must be determined in accordance with a methodology solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The gainsharing methodology may account for the relative amount of CJR‑X activities provided by a collaborator versus others when determining amounts paid, but selection of collaborators or opportunity to make/receive payments must not be based on volume or value of referrals or business. CMS considered broader standards but proposes to follow CJR and TEAM methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on aggregate gainsharing payments
rubrics_metrics.description: For each performance year, the aggregate amount of all gainsharing payments derived from a reconciliation payment by the CJR‑X participant must not exceed the reconciliation payment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures gainsharing does not exceed available reconciliation funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and recovery related to gainsharing
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant must not make gainsharing payments to a collaborator subject to action for noncompliance by CMS or other federal/state entities, or for provision of substandard care; sharing arrangements must require recovery of any gainsharing payment that contained funds from a CMS overpayment or was based on false or fraudulent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program‑integrity safeguard to prevent payments to entities with compliance or quality issues and to ensure recovery where payments were improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment payment timing and precondition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment payments from a CJR‑X collaborator to a CJR‑X participant may be made at any agreed interval, but must not be issued prior to CMS calculation of the repayment amount and cannot be assessed in the absence of a repayment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CJR‑X participant must not receive any amounts under a sharing arrangement other than alignment payments as defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate limits on alignment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate alignment payments received by the CJR‑X participant from all collaborators must not exceed 50 percent of the participant's repayment amount for a performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further limits: alignment payments from a collaborator other than an ACO may not exceed 25 percent of the participant's repayment amount; alignment payments from a collaborator that is an ACO may not exceed 50 percent of the repayment amount. Rationale: ensure participant retains significant portion of repayment responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and traceability of gainsharing and alignment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: All gainsharing and alignment payments must be administered by the CJR‑X participant in accordance with GAAP and Government Auditing Standards (The Yellow Book) and must be made by check, electronic funds transfer, or another traceable cash transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes an EFT requirement could impose burdens on small providers and proposes payment methods to mitigate administrative burdens that could discourage participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements for sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must meet a variety of documentation requirements to ensure the integrity of sharing arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes documentation and record‑retention obligations and monitoring access for CMS; specific documentation requirements are included in the continuing proposed rule text (referenced at §512.670 and monitoring/compliance provisions).
